newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk insurance company Ray Sigorta to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turk insurance company Ray Sigorta to float shares.

text.p: Turkish insurance company Ray Sigorta A.S. will float 15 percent of its capital in a two-day initial public offer beginning on July 17, the company said in newspaper advertisements.

The fixed price will be 5,500 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-value share in the offer to be lead-managed by brokerage houses Turk Ekonomi Bankasi Yatirim and co-led by Is Yatirim ve Menkul Degerler. The consortium includes four other intermediaries.

Ray Sigorta will offer 98.55 billion lira worth of shares from its current 657 billion lira capital. Of the total offer, 25 percent will be allocated to investors based abroad and 15 percent to domestic institutional investors.
Istanbul-based Ray Sigorta is owned by Turkey's media and finance group Dogan Holding A.S..
The company's net profits rose by 83 percent to 178.8 billion lira in the first quarter of 1997, from 97.7 billion in the same period last year.
Its total premium collections rose 93.4 percent to 1.77 trillion lira in the first three months, from 915 billion in the same period in 1996.
